summary: This note is a clipped Wikipedia-style history of the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic (RSFSR), covering its founding in 1917, renamings, territorial changes, union in the USSR in 1922, and its transformation into the Russian Federation in December 1991. It also covers the Soviet-era government titles and the political events of 1990-1991, including Yeltsin's decrees against the Communist Party and the Belavezha Accords. The content is somewhat repetitive and contains some duplicated dates and sentences across sections.
one_line: History of the Russian SFSR, from its 1917 founding and 1922 Soviet union to its 1991 transformation into the Russian Federation.
key_facts: The Soviet regime first came to power on November 7, 1917, immediately after the Russian Provisional Government was overthrown in the October Revolution.
On January 25, 1918, the All-Russian Congress of Soviets renamed the unrecognized state the Soviet Russian Republic.
The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk was signed on March 3, 1918, giving away much of the land of the former Russian Empire to Germany.
On December 30, 1922, Russia was united with the Ukrainian, Byelorussian and Transcaucasian Soviet republics into the Soviet Union via the Treaty on the Creation of the USSR.
The final Soviet name for the republic, the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic, was adopted in the Soviet Constitution of 1936.
On April 17, 1946, the Kaliningrad Oblast, the northern portion of the former German province of East Prussia, was annexed by the Soviet Union and made part of the Russian SFSR.
On June 12, 1990, the Congress of People's Deputies adopted the Declaration of State Sovereignty of the Russian SFSR, beginning the 'War of Laws'.
On June 12, 1991, Boris Yeltsin was elected the first President.
On August 23, after the failure of GKChP, Yeltsin signed a decree suspending all activity by the Communist Party of the Russian SFSR in the territory of Russia.
On November 6, Yeltsin banned the Communist Parties of the USSR and the RSFSR from the territory of the RSFSR.
On December 8, 1991, heads of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus signed the Belavezha Accords, declaring the dissolution of the USSR and establishing the CIS.
On December 12, 1991, the Russian Parliament ratified the agreement, and the Russian SFSR denounced the 1922 Treaty on the Creation of the USSR.
On December 25, 1991, just hours after Gorbachev resigned, the Russian SFSR was renamed the Russian Federation (Russia).
The Government was known as the Council of People's Commissars (1917–1946), Council of Ministers (1946–1978) and Council of Ministers–Government (1978–1991).
In 1943, Karachay Autonomous Oblast was dissolved by Joseph Stalin after the Karachays were exiled to Central Asia for alleged collaboration with the Germans.
